question: In a chloraminated system, which water quality change is an early input signal that nitrification may be starting in a warm storage tank?
correctAnswer: Falling chloramine residual with rising nitrite in the tank water
explanation: Nitrifying bacteria consume chloramine and produce nitrite, so a falling residual paired with rising nitrite is an early warning sign.
options: Rising chloramine residual with falling nitrite in the tank water
Falling chloramine residual with rising nitrite in the tank water
Falling water temperature with rising pressure in the tank water
Rising turbidity with falling alkalinity measured in the tank water
optionA: Rising chloramine residual with falling nitrite in the tank water
optionB: Falling chloramine residual with rising nitrite in the tank water
optionC: Falling water temperature with rising pressure in the tank water
optionD: Rising turbidity with falling alkalinity measured in the tank water
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: nitrification awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Before a repaired main section is returned to service, which step comes after the section has been disinfected and flushed?
correctAnswer: Collecting bacteriological samples and waiting for acceptable results before normal use
explanation: Disinfection and flushing are followed by bacteriological sampling, and the section is returned to normal service only after acceptable results.
options: Opening every service on the section and waiting for pressure complaints from customers
Backfilling the trench fully and waiting for settlement before any sampling is attempted
Collecting bacteriological samples and waiting for acceptable results before normal use
Raising system pressure above normal and waiting for hydrant flows to clear the section
optionA: Opening every service on the section and waiting for pressure complaints from customers
optionB: Backfilling the trench fully and waiting for settlement before any sampling is attempted
optionC: Collecting bacteriological samples and waiting for acceptable results before normal use
optionD: Raising system pressure above normal and waiting for hydrant flows to clear the section
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: disinfection of repaired mains. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: When opening a hydrant for a flow test, which sequence protects the main from a pressure surge?
correctAnswer: Open the hydrant slowly until it is fully open and flow has steadied
explanation: Opening a hydrant slowly avoids a sudden pressure change that can surge through the main and damage pipes or services.
options: Open the hydrant slowly until it is fully open and flow has steadied
Open the hydrant quickly until it is fully open and flow has steadied
Open the hydrant halfway, then close it quickly to seat the main valve
Open the hydrant fully, then throttle it back using the operating nut
optionA: Open the hydrant slowly until it is fully open and flow has steadied
optionB: Open the hydrant quickly until it is fully open and flow has steadied
optionC: Open the hydrant halfway, then close it quickly to seat the main valve
optionD: Open the hydrant fully, then throttle it back using the operating nut

question: A new subdivision sits about 40 metres higher than the rest of a pressure zone. Which consequence should the operator expect at those homes?
correctAnswer: Lower service pressures, especially during periods of high demand in the zone
explanation: Higher elevation leaves less pressure head, so elevated homes see lower pressures that drop further when demand is high.
options: Higher service pressures, especially during periods of high demand in the zone
Equal service pressures at all times, because elevation does not affect pressure
Frequent pressure relief valve openings at the homes during overnight low demand
Lower service pressures, especially during periods of high demand in the zone
optionA: Higher service pressures, especially during periods of high demand in the zone
optionB: Equal service pressures at all times, because elevation does not affect pressure
optionC: Frequent pressure relief valve openings at the homes during overnight low demand
optionD: Lower service pressures, especially during periods of high demand in the zone

Flush only the service lines on the street until each customer reports clearer water
Flush the storage tank overflow until the tank level drops by a small set amount daily

Lower the water level in every storage tank and wait for the pattern to reverse itself
Increase monitoring at storage and dead end sites and check nitrite and nitrate levels
Switch all sampling sites to a single downtown location and compare results each month

question: Two pressure zones are separated by a closed boundary valve. Which effect follows if that valve is opened by mistake?
correctAnswer: Water flows from the higher pressure zone into the lower pressure zone
explanation: Water moves from higher head to lower head, so opening a boundary valve lets the higher zone feed and possibly overpressurize the lower zone.
options: Water flows from the lower pressure zone into the higher pressure zone
Water flows from the higher pressure zone into the lower pressure zone
Water stops flowing in both zones until a booster pump is started again
Water quality samples in both zones become invalid for the rest of the year
optionA: Water flows from the lower pressure zone into the higher pressure zone
optionB: Water flows from the higher pressure zone into the lower pressure zone
optionC: Water stops flowing in both zones until a booster pump is started again
optionD: Water quality samples in both zones become invalid for the rest of the year

Lower chloramine feed at the plant and extend sampling intervals at high age areas
Close boundary valves between zones and hold water in tanks for longer periods weekly

Open the hydrant a second time briefly so the barrel refills and stays warmer overnight
Spread gravel over the hydrant base so melt water soaks away before the next cold night
